The evidence explicitly states that the algorithm is optimized by 'keeping block lookups within the current working chunk to avoid repeated chunk boundary calculations.' It details the use of bitwise operations (bit-shifting `>> 5` and masking `& 0x1f`) to determine chunk indices and relative positions, contrasting this with the 'original ray marching algorithm' which 'worked with map-relative positions' and had to 'calculate which chunk the block belonged to' every time. This supports the claim that the method replaces global coordinate arithmetic (or repeated global lookups) with bitwise operations for chunk indexing to reduce computational overhead.
